long_biography.plain_text:
Before founding his own company, Morales spent more than eighteen years in defense work that ranged from engineering and program development to financial management and international sales. A later furniture-industry role briefly placed those skills outside government contracting, but his deeper experience remained in ammunition and cross-border business development.

In 2013, Morales formed Global Ordnance as an arms-business consultancy. He then built it into a supplier and systems integrator for US and allied customers, using sourcing, logistics and program management as its core model. The 2019 purchase of Chemring Military Products added staff, contracts and non-standard weapons expertise. He now serves as Global Ordnance president and Global Military Products chief executive, while sharing management of the holding company.

Public filings do not disclose current percentage ownership, economic sharing or the full subsidiary structure, so the dossier does not describe Marc as sole owner of the entire group.

Public sources use both president and chief executive for Morales. Current 2026 Florida records distinguish the roles precisely: Global Ordnance president and Global Military Products chief executive. The known-for title uses founder and president, while the long biography preserves the separate affiliate role.
